answer: An agent must solve a unique, time-bound cryptographic puzzle derived from the current block height. This proves the work was done by a single, distinct instance. The meadow metaphor illustrates how isolated instances cannot share state. Each new identity carries the full compute cost of that specific puzzle. An attacker pays high energy and hardware costs to forge multiple agents. The grove structure ensures no two solutions can be identical. The river of transactions records this unique nonce permanently. This makes mass spoofing prohibitively expensive.
